definitions.meaning: an ace is a top performer and clubs are what a golfer swings, so a champion with the clubs
one of the fifty-two in a standard pack, the top-ranking one of the black trefoil suit

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is a master of golf clubs; as a whole it names a playing card in a standard deck.

clue.text: About to cut, cut into small pieces

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of slicing something and then dices it finely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'on the point of' but gives C (circa); 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing grinds food with the teeth into smaller bits.

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
a ford is a shallow place to cross a river

explanation.surface: A tidy stretch of water is crossed near a university campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' suggests tidy, but it is the old word for cattle, giving OX.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford is the name of an ancient English seat of learning.

clue.text: Cares about Edward doubled up with laughter

indicators.note: about means the letters of the word cares are turned around into a new order

parts.note: Ed is the short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Someone worries over Edward, who is bent double laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CARES into CREAS, then ED follows. In British slang to be creased is to be helpless with laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this word for someone folded over in fits of mirth.

clue.text: One you knit from the sound of it

indicators.note: tells the solver that the words you knit, said out loud, give the entry

parts.note: the two words spoken quickly sound like a single word for one item

explanation.surface: Someone knits a single thing, by the sound of what they say.
explanation.definitionFit: A single item or quantity of one is called this in measurement and counting.

parts.note: so and as both compare, as in 'not so big' and 'not as big'
licit means lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: A lawyer is sought after because they are legal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at a solicitor, but 'as' gives SO and 'legal' gives LICIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to ask for or try to obtain something.

definitions.meaning: indirect or not straightforward, as a route or explanation
a circular junction where vehicles all travel the same direction round a central island

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both indirect and a circular road junction where traffic goes one way around.

parts.note: a night worker sleeps and dreams in daylight hours, and an unrealistic person is a fantasist

explanation.definitionFit: A fantasist lost in reverie is one, and literally so is someone who sleeps through daylight after working nights.

clue.text: Fusses about what to add to the whisky

definitions.text: what to add to the whisky

indicators.note: about means the word for fusses is turned around back to front

parts.note: ados are fusses, as in much ado

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss about what mixer should go into their whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy water is a classic mixer splashed into Scotch.

clue.text: One does not have to practise it

definitions.text: One does not have to practise it

parts.words: One does not have to practise it
parts.note: reads like an optional exercise, but means a person refuses themselves things in order to practise it

explanation.definitionFit: Going without, by refusing oneself pleasures, is abstinence or austerity.

parts.note: read as de-creased, with wrinkles taken out of clothes in the household

explanation.definitionFit: Pressing laundry with a hot appliance smooths out its wrinkles.

clue.text: Old penny fairy tale character accepted for inaugural gift

indicators.note: the character takes in, or accepts, the coin within his name

parts.note: Hansel is the boy in the Grimm tale with Gretel
D was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A storybook character takes an old coin as a first present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted' puts D, the old British penny from Latin denarius, inside HANSEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsel is an old word for a gift marking a new start, like a new year or venture.

parts.note: the opposite of down is high, so a street that is not down is a lofty one

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the main shopping road of a town is traditionally called this.
explanation.definitionFit: British towns name their principal retail road this way.

definitions.meaning: full of suspense, keeping one on edge
a nervous practice of chewing at the fingertips

explanation.definitionFit: Tense drama makes people gnaw their fingertips, which is also the name of that nervous practice.

clue.text: Weapon for knight who has lost a lot

indicators.note: the knight's name lets go of part of itself, so letters are removed

parts.note: Lancelot is a knight of the Round Table
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weapon belonging to a knight who has suffered heavy losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lost' takes LOT from LANCELOT, the Arthurian knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pointed pole carried by mounted knights.

indicators.note: read as re-sort: the letters of seaside are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: A holiday town by the sea has something to grumble about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seaside resort' reads as a holiday town, but 'resort' is re-sort, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an illness or ailment.

parts.note: golfers swinging a club gouge a piece of turf from the golf course

explanation.definitionFit: A chunk of turf gouged out by a golfer's stroke.

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of vat I'd are broken up and put back differently

explanation.surface: Someone lifts a vat they had damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A small crane on a ship used for lowering lifeboats is a kind of lifting gear.

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the word for complain is dropped

parts.note: to gripe is to complain

explanation.surface: Someone moans on and on about the handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' reads as nonstop moaning but clips the E off GRIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is the part you hold, the hold or grasp.

clue.text: Class for a very large number

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A school class with a huge number of pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: British schools call a class or year group by this name.

parts.note: a man of many talents, but here a man who plays roles on stage

explanation.definitionFit: A stage performer takes roles, or parts.

definitions.meaning: split into three words it asks whether I can do something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means good-natured, and split up it asks whether the speaker is capable.

clue.text: It purifies again of better quality

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
finer means of higher quality

explanation.surface: Something purifies again to give a better product.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant or person that removes impurities, as from sugar or oil.

clue.text: It is so delightful under the tree

parts.note: sub is the Latin-derived prefix for under
the lime is a tree, also called the linden

explanation.surface: Sitting beneath the tree is wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Supremely lovely or exalted, beyond mere pleasantness.

indicators.note: round means the letters of rattles go round into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A satellite rattles as it orbits.
explanation.definitionFit: Telstar was the first satellite to relay live television across the Atlantic.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the river's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
taken as written

explanation.surface: Travelling upstream, a man might get worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reverses TEES, the English river, to SEET; 'might' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To churn or boil inwardly with anger.

clue.text: It is sensitive to light in tear-jerker

indicators.note: the letters of in tear are jerked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Something light-sensitive appears in a weepy film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear-jerker' reads as a weepy film, but 'jerker' shakes up IN TEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The layer at the back of the eye that receives images.

clue.text: Young woman whose prosperity is assured, we hear

indicators.note: signals that a word is spoken, and what is heard gives the entry

parts.note: someone with success guaranteed is said to be made, as in 'a made man'

explanation.surface: A young woman whose fortune is secured, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a girl or unmarried young woman.

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the words calibre respected

explanation.surface: A brother within another highly respected figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Brer is dialect for brother, as in Brer Rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Southern US dialect form for a brother, from the Uncle Remus tales.

clue.text: Sudden inspiration by cup holder in rage

parts.note: a bra holds the cups of the breasts
taken as written
a storm is an outburst of rage

explanation.surface: A bright idea about a drinks holder, arrived at in a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cup holder' suggests a drinks stand, but it is a bra.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever idea.

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of Rene are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman named Rene upset the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea eagle is a crossword staple.

parts.note: older plus berry, a soft fruit that is literally more mature

explanation.definitionFit: Small dark fruit of the sambucus shrub, used in wine and cordial.
